text_fidelity_a:
StarTech.com Dual Monitor USB 3.0 Laptop Docking Station with HDMI & DVI/VGA, 6x USB-A Hub, GbE, Audio, Universal Type-A Dock - Windows/macOS/ChromeOS (USB3SDOCKHD) I had high hopes for this docking station from StarTech but, thus far, I’ve been pretty disappointed.

Like many people I like the portability of working from a laptop but when I am at my workstation I want more screen space to work on - I thought this Docking Station would be a perfect solution. Well, in theory, it would.

Inside the box you’ll find the docking station, a 3.0 USB cable, a power adapter with snap on plugs to fit various world power sources, a DVI to VGA adapter, and a CD-ROM.

Unlike many docking stations or hubs this is not Plug and Play. I’m running the most updated Windows 10 64bit and the CD-ROM is completely useless. After inserting it in my computer I received a message reading that it was not compatible with my machine. No problem, I went to the manufacturer’s website, found the product, clicked on support, downloaded the zip file containing the setup and updated drivers for my OS and continued.

I went through the installation process and it appeared to install fine. After accepting the user agreement it checked my system for compatibility - finding no issues it continued and completed installation. I went to device manager and noticed an error in USB connected devices but figured with a restart it would correct.

I restarted but the error remains. Configuration Descriptor Request Failed - Windows has stopped device. I have uninstalled and reinstalled, searched help, used Windows Update to search for a better driver - so far nothing has worked.

In regards to functionality - the USB ports (two 3.0 and four 2.0) all function without issue and the Ethernet Port works great providing me over 200Mb/s. Due to not having the correct drivers I’ve been unable to test the multiple monitor capabilities.

I have contacted tech support and as of writing I have not heard back. If they are able to help me solve these issues I will update my review to reflect my further findings.

It appears this Docking Station is outdated being developed for older operating systems and while it may work for some users, others will find it needlessly difficult.

I would look at more recently manufactured docking stations that have been developed with the current operating systems - especially if you are using Windows 10.
text_fidelity_b: StarTech.com Dual Monitor USB 3.0 Laptop Docking Station with HDMI & DVI/VGA, 6x USB-A Hub, GbE, Audio, Universal Type-A Dock - Windows/macOS/ChromeOS (USB3SDOCKHD)

PROS: These are super light weight stands that will prop up pretty much any phone or tablet. They are adequate for their purpose. The stand can be adjusted to any position, and the spot that the device rests on is generous. Small, light and easy to carry around these have convenience in portability. Also, as I have the multi pack, you can place them all over or share. Or lose some, haha. Best value is multi pack. Single price is too much for quality of this product.

CONS: They claim anti-skid, but it fails in that feature. So lightweight that if you intend to tap at your device often, depending on what surface you have this placed on, it will scoot around some. I recommend modifying it with a couple beads (or line) of hot glue to give it a rubbery bottom. Or use a scrap of rug pad (that non slip material), or simply use it on a less smooth/hard surface. If just needing to prop up phone or tablet, then it will stay put. The kickstand is solid.

I am most comfortable using it on a smaller device if only because these have barely any weight to them. I have a much heavier stand that I prefer to use, but the price for one is significant. These are basic, light weight and super budget friendly (for multi pack).

Would make for a good stocking stuffer!

In my pics, I am demonstrating this product with pixel phone and LGtablet
text_fidelity_b: Elimoons Phone Stand,4 Pack Multi-Angle Cell Phone Stand Tablet Stand Universal Smartphones for Holder Tablets(6-11),e-Reader,Compatible Phone XS/XR/8/8 Plus/7/7 Plus/11,Galaxy S8/S7

Bose QuietComfort 35 II Wireless Bluetooth Headphones, Noise-Cancelling, with Alexa Voice Control - Black Bose has been and remains the best headphone maker. I’ve tried at least a dozen different products on amazon, with perhaps a dozen more in my life, and in all those experiences, the Bose name always stood far ahead of the crowd.

First, their noise cancelling technology remains the best. Eerily effective, especially on airplanes and in cars, trains, or buses, you put them on, and the world becomes quieter, making you realize how terrible the ambient noise was! These have the added benefit of adjustable noise cancellation, unlike previous models.

In comfort, these are built for long-term use, remaining wearable for hours. Most other headphones I’ve tried tend to make your ears sore, but not these! They feel soft and lovely everywhere they land on your head.

With or without Bluetooth, these offer exceptional clarity of sound, powerful bass, and clear crisp treble, none of which turn to distorted noise, even at high volumes. Yes, these are very powerful! And they offer the option for wireless battery-operated use or plug-in use. They sound equally good in either setting. As for battery life, these won’t let you down. They last hours and hours without needing a charge.

My partner has the QuietComfort 30, I believe, and I always loved borrowing those, so it’s great having a pair of my own (in an even better version, no less!)

Fantastic! No product compares to Bose.

Transcend 16 GB Class 6 SDHC Flash Memory Card TS16GSDHC6 I have been using Panasonic SDHC Class 6 4GB cards, and have been pretty happy with them. I decided to get this one just because of the low price and high ratings, and am pleased to find that I agree with the many 5-star reviews.

Some information I didn't see in the other reviews, in case it's of interest: I ran a write test with a big file on my computer, and saw write speeds consistently above 6MB/s, as you ought to expect for a Class 6. (Among other things, that means of course that your camera can get ready for the next shot just that much faster because it's spending less time waiting for the recording to be completed.)

I didn't bother with a read test, since read speed is rarely an issue.

A comment on SD card readers/writers. As many have said, older SD devices, including older cameras, will not work with SDHC cards. My old card adapter (Sandisk 8-in-1) hung when I put this chip in. But my newer adapters (a built-in slot, and an Edge All-in-1) worked just fine. So if you're having trouble, this is possibly the first thing to check.

Computer Speakers for Desktop/Laptop/Mac, USB Powered PC Speaker, 2.0 Channel Stereo Multimedia Speaker for TV, Notebook, Built-in Diaphragm,3w3w Horn and in-Line Volume Control TOMOT FT-165 There's a lot I really like about these. Let me start off by pointing out, however, these are NOT USB SPEAKERS. They are simply powered off USB and use a standard headphone jack as the audio input. I have to admit, at first I was taken aback by how small they are, and assumed they must produce weak sound as a result (I'm used to a set of Harmon/Kardon speakers on my desktop which are bigger than these). But despite their size, they actually produce a really great and full sound, with an almost exaggerated stereo effect thanks to individual speakers pointing in different directions.
What I love most about it, however, is that it is USB powered. That means no additional plugs needed on my desktop, and in fact they are fantastic for boosting the audio on a laptop. In the included picture I'm posting with this, I have an old Dell Laptop that my kids use to watch things on, and these sound FAR better than the tiny built in laptop speaker. Since it is USB powered, it can be simply be run directly off the laptop itself, no additional wires or outlets necessary. Put one plug into an available USB slot, the other into the headphone jack. It makes a nice and neat looking portable setup. The thing is, I can't help but wonder why it isn't just a 100% USB sound system? I have a pair of headphones that I love using that are completely digital- it identifies as its own sound card when plugged in and requires only that one USB plug. I sort of assumed that this would be something similar to that and therefore require only that ONE plug to operate. In some cases, the digital sound systems are better than analog plug ones (interference, for example) anyway, so it seems strange to have an analog speaker system powered by a digital USB port. But I guess there can be interesting uses for this too.
For example, a device like an older phone with a headphone jack can connect to this which wouldn't work with USB. Or enhancing the speaker of an Echo Dot and powering it off a dual USB outlet (one for the Dot, the other for the speakers). It is definitely an interesting and useful thing to have around! And for the price, color me impressed!
text_fidelity_b: Computer Speakers for Desktop/Laptop/Mac, USB Powered PC Speaker, 2.0 Channel Stereo Multimedia Speaker for TV, Notebook, Built-in Diaphragm,3w3w Horn and in-Line Volume Control TOMOT FT-165

Belkin N150 Wireless USB Adapter with up to 150Mbps Link Rate We have several networked devices in our house and also several individualized networks configured. Not all of the networks can be seen by all devices so I looked to this Belkin USB WiFi adapter to allow one of the older computer systems to access the most reliable network in the house - a 5GHz network that only one or two of the systems can see.

Installation was a snap. I popped in the CD, told it to install the drivers and we were off to the races. The particular target system was a 32-bit Windows Vista laptop. After just a couple of minutes the driver was completely installed and when I plugged in the USB adapter is was picked up immediately. I could see the desired network as well as several other networks in the neighborhood that were previously invisible to the computer. I shut off the built-in adapter, connected to the 5GHz network and went to the net.

So far, the connection has been very stable and speeds have been excellent. The router to which it is connected is a TP-Link router and so far we have seen no issues between the two devices. I have not had this adapter very long so it is still early to say it’s completely stable but all indicators up to this point have been very favorable.

Several other reviewers have mentioned that this adapter does not work with Linux. This is true - there are no drivers available for this adapter other than for Windows XP/Vista/7/8. If you need an adapter that will allow you to connect a Linux or Mac system to a wireless network, this is not the device you need right now.

So far I can’t find too much about which to complain concerning this router. It seems to be stable and reliable on the system to which it is attached here. I am satisfied with it and based on my experience with it can recommend it - if you’re sticking with Windows.
text_fidelity_b: Belkin N150 Wireless USB Adapter with up to 150Mbps Link Rate

Logitech M570 Wireless Trackball Mouse – Ergonomic Design with Sculpted Right-Hand Shape, Compatible with Apple Mac / Microsoft, USB Unifying Receiver, Dark Gray (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I prefer trackballs to mice and I have been looking for a good wireless trackball as my primary system is a laptop. In the past I had a Logitech TrackMan II, a hideous device that made my hands hurt. Logitech's new M570 trackball is far and away better than that TrackMan II, and I would consider it an excellent device except for one thing.

I have large hands, and as a consequence I need larger pointing devices to fit my hand. The M570 is marginally larger than my standard mouse which gave me pause right off the bat, but my concerns were unfounded. Even though this trackball device is not especially large, it fits my hand comfortably and I can spin the ball with ease without cramping my hands. My finger tips rest on the buttons and my thumb tip rests on the ball, while the fleshy part of my palm is on the desk past the plastic base. Finally, a trackball that fits my hand much like a normal mouse.

I have a marble mouse and while it's a decent trackball-like device, the ball easily drops out when the device is inverted and as a result I have dropped the ball one too many times and chipped it. The M570 holds the ball in place and does not allow it to simply come out without applying deliberate pressure, resulting in less opportunities to either lose or damage the ball.

The ball itself is a pretty shade of blue and, with the exception of the finger holes, looks a lot like a miniature bowling ball.

The M570 has 4 buttons and a scroll wheel that can be pressed for a total of 5 programmable buttons. The one problem with this trackball involves the scroll wheel - there is no horizontal scroll. While this is really just an inconvenience, horizontal scrolling has become very commonplace and that it is not included is a disappointment.

The range on the M570 us excellent. I am able to control the pointer on the screen from a distance of 15' - 20' away without any issues at all (except that it's harder to read the screen). This is very convenient and will be immeasurably helpful for presentations where the desk is a good distance from the computer and control is needed across that distance.

I am very pleased with the Logitech M570 wireless trackball and can heartily recommend it. The one improvement would be horizontal scrolling; otherwise, this trackball is superb.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech M570 Wireless Trackball Mouse – Ergonomic Design with Sculpted Right-Hand Shape, Compatible with Apple Mac / Microsoft, USB Unifying Receiver, Dark Gray (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Brainwavz R3 Dual Dynamic Driver Earphones (V2) I use earbuds a lot since I typically prefer the lightness and ease of use compared with traditional headphones. Right out of the box these were a bit puzzling as to how to position them for use. But, after a bit of fiddling with the over-the-ear loop, it becomes clear.

The in-ear comfort is good. It comes with a variety of ear tips including two types I’ve not used before: a double flange silicon tip and a triple flange silicon tip. The flanges allow the ear bud to make a much better seal in your ear canal. That not only helps cut out ambient noise intruding, it also improves the bass response. I found the double flange works best for me, but the variety of tips included appears sufficient to fit pretty much any ear.

It also comes with an excellent case for storage, and adapters for airplane use and for 1/4 inch plugs. I especially like the case since it’s small enough to make it easy to carry along (roughly 3.5 inches by 3 by 1.5 inches thick) and is reinforced to avoid being crushed. It has mesh pockets to keep everything stowed, and looks nice to boot (black with red contrast in the middle). All-in-all, it’s a great kit in terms of useful accessories.

I’m not as pleased with the cord. While I like how sturdy it is, it has a “Y” link that always seems to be in the way when I’m working out. I got used to it eventually, but a more streamlined cord system would have been a better design approach. Another negative is the 3.5mm plug. It needs to be seated just so or you get sound cut-outs or static. I tried it with several devices to be sure the issue is with the plug and not the device. A more robust plug is needed for this – you shouldn’t have to fiddle with it to get it to seat properly.

The over-the-ear loops are also a bit annoying at first. Granted, that’s certainly due to the fact that I usually use standard in-ear buds without the loop, so any type of loop feels weird to me at first. The material is soft and bendy, so you can position it in any variety of ways. It could benefit from some additional padding. On the plus side, they do hold the buds in very well. Quick head movements that would have loosened an in-ear bud didn’t jar these loose at all.

Now for the really important feature: how they sound. In a word, excellent. My benchmark for moderately-priced earbuds has been units made by RHA out of the UK. These sound nearly as good. Very clean sound but still ample bass provided that you select the right tip. For me, the standard tip (the one installed as delivered) gave me very little in terms of bass. Selecting a different tip to provide a better ear fit did wonders for bass response.

They are a bit more airy than the RHA sound. That could be a plus or a minus depending on your preferred type of music. Very heavy bass music is not a good match for these. Pretty much everything else is, and I appreciated the enhanced clarity. It’s the type of sound that, when you hear it, the first word that would come to mind is “clean.”

They look odd, make take you a moment to figure out how to position them, but provide a very open, natural sound. It comes with a well-designed kit of useful extras. However, the plug issues, the cord, and the ear loops collectively knock it down a star. Still well worth considering, however, and I would certainly recommend them.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Brainwavz R3 Dual Dynamic Driver Earphones (V2)

This plastic Otterbox uses is so very rigid, the protective cover is extremely difficult to pop on and off. When kiddo’s alarm goes off and he’s already off somewhere, it takes me ages to get the thing open to shut it down. I also can’t find the power or volume buttons easily by touch, they blend in so much.

What’s outright laughable is the kickstand. It’s on the inside of the cover that you take off, so you set the iPad on it. It doesn’t sit very securely at all, and now that this model has the pencil holder, in some positions it won’t stay up - it teeter totters right over! So no, it’s not a 4 position kickstand, but a 3 position. The whole situation is anything but stable, so if there’s a tug on a charger or headphone cord, instead of just sliding a tiny bit on the table or not doing anything at all, it slips off the kickstand and ... well, this is how we already know it’s sturdy, as the thing ended up on the floor more times in the first day than the iPad did in a year in its old case.

It’s quite heavy compared to other choices that offer similar protection, and very very difficult to install. I am never need to read directions type, and these directions were meaningless. It required a YouTube and a lot of swearing, plus a sliced open cuticle, to get it on. Even then it didn’t seat properly around the speakers and needed quite a bit of poking into place with a toothpick.

I sincerely hope there will be a day when there’s another rugged iPad mini case, with a kickstand and a shell that goes over the screen. Because this just doesn’t cut it.

text_fidelity_a:
Leather Centric 15 Inch Buffalo Leather Laptop Messenger Bag Office Briefcase College Bag Fits Upto 14 Inch This bag arrived just before we went out of town for a trip, and the timing couldn’t have been better. My wife has a 13” laptop that she loves and uses daily, and this bag was the perfect solution for carrying it on the trip. It isn’t necessarily the most fancy bag but it gets the job done and it seems to be made well. I would make one alteration to make it better, based on experiences I have had with similar bags in the past.

This is a smaller bag, not designed to hold 15.6” or larger laptops, so it is not going to help people who have “standard” laptop sizes unless this is going to be used as a book bag instead. If you need a bag that fits a laptop that is 15.6” or greater, this one will not work for you. That’s okay as it is very clearly marketed as such so it should come as no surprise. Being for smaller computers doesn’t make it useless though; it does work very well as a book bag and an organizer, so even if you need a larger one for your computer this one has its uses.

This is a leather messenger bag. The leather is a style I have heard referred to as “ruined leather” though that’s not an indicator of the quality. On the contrary, this bag is well made and I can’t find anything about it to suggest that it is made with less care and quality than the price dictates. In spite of the appearance, the materials are quality and I cannot find any blemishes or cuts, the stitching is straight and all the clasps and zippers work properly.

There are plenty of pockets to store your items and keep organized. Of course there this the main compartment which is designed to hold a computer, but there is room for books as well in the main compartment. There are zippered compartments inside the bag as well as outside, and these are good for carrying your mouse, pens and pencils, passport, maps and other important items.

The flap that covers the main compartment secures to the rest of the bag with straps that fasten with a pressure snap behind a fake decorative buckle, and this represents the one thing about this bag I do not like. If you are not careful and you catch one of the straps on something will walking, you can break the snap and damage or ruin the bag. I have had this happen with other bags using this kind of fastener. I would rather see a magnet used instead which will let go when pulled, or get rid of the decorative buckle and replace it with a real buckle which will hold regardless.

I like this bag. It is well made and it should last for years with proper care. It has room for your smaller laptop as well as books and other supplies. I don’t like the way the flap secures, mainly because if problems I have had with similar bags using similar fasteners, but for the majority of users this is a good solution that is worth consideration. It’s a little more expensive than a canvas bag, but it should last longer.
text_fidelity_b: Leather Centric 15 Inch Buffalo Leather Laptop Messenger Bag Office Briefcase College Bag Fits Upto 14 Inch

Garmin nüvi 1350LMT 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer)) I drive in and around the Boston area, where none of the streets run north/south or east/west, every other intersection is a rotary, and a wrong turn down a one way street can take you an hour to correct.

The Nuvi is slightly better than trying to drive with a map on your steering wheel. I have been using mine for awhile now, and it mostly gets me where I want to go.

The problem is mostly how it does it. As many have already noted, there is no easy way to get it to show you alternate routes. And out of the city, especially, the route it gives you can be full of surprises. Take you off the highway and onto a dirt road for no reason whatsoever surprises. That happened to my husband on his way to a job in Hartford.

And forget trying to get around traffic. I was using it to get home from a doctor's office and saw that there was a ton of traffic on the route it was giving me through Harvard Square, so I turned toward another way home - one I do not know as well, but I know it is possible to get home that way - expecting the Nuvi to tell me it was recalculating and give me my next turn.

It did so, and I turned and followed the directions each time as it - get this - took me into the Harvard Business School parking lot and then out onto a one way street that put me on a no-turning-back 100% committed course to the traffic in Harvard Square.

Thanks, Nuvi.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nüvi 1350LMT 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer))

Until we moved to a new house. The arris modem was dropping signal significantly every single day - we either had super slow or no connection for hours. I had the cable guys out here four times in 61 days to fix the problem. I was literally ready to just cancel Suddenlink and move to AT&T for internet, but decided to try this Nighthawk combo first.

It was spotted instantly by Suddenlink when I called to give them the new modem Mac address, so the connection was just a single phone call to start. No drama. I have 9 daily devices on WiFi and three TiVo receivers that connect via Ethernet or WiFi plus the land line phone. There's four Ethernet connections and two phone connections on the modem, plenty for our needs.

It's been almost three weeks and I've noticed an astonishing improvement in our initial connection and reliability. Rather than daily outages, we have had five total in three weeks and none lasted more than 15 to 20 minutes. Stability of the signal has improved and our speeds are double what they were with the arris modem - we're actually getting the high speed service we pay for. The router is also projecting the WiFi far enough that I no longer need to use a secondary extender to get WiFi by the pool and patio.

I like the Genie app with this. The ability to check channels, reboot the router if needed, and see which devices are online is very handy. I also like the clear, bright lights on the front. At a glance you know if there's a problem. Bottom line for me is that I haven't canceled our services from Suddenlink because this unit fixed 90% of our problem.

Seagate 600 SSD 480 GB SATA 6 Gb/s 2.5-Inch 7mm Z-Height Solid State Drive ST480HM000 Though I have a laptop, I decided to use this solid-state drive as a boot drive on my desktop computer. If you are unfamiliar with the difference between a solid-state and a regular hard drive, the solid-state has no moving parts, which makes it silent, fast, reliable, and shock resistant. It has twice the capacity and twice the speed of the solid-state drive I got a couple of years ago for the same price, and blows away a standard drive for speed.

Given the silence and speed, it makes a great boot drive for running Windows, Photoshop, and other programs where speed is a huge advantage. Just to give you an idea, when upgrading from a regular two-year-old hard drive to this solid-state drive, my Windows boot time went from two minutes to about 10 seconds. Seriously, my computer now starts up and is ready to use in like 10 seconds.

What I do is use a solid-state drive as my boot drive and a regular hard drive as a storage drive. Solid-state drives like this are really expensive to purchase if you need any kind of capacity, but a 200 GB drive will certainly hold all of your programs and often used files.

As for this drive specifically, I hooked it up to my desktop and it was immediately recognized by Windows. The drivers installed automatically. In order to make the drive show up as a drive and work in Windows 7, I had to right-click on computer, click manage, double-click storage, double-click disk management, partition it, give it a drive letter, and format it.

As I said, it's a lot faster than the solid-state drive I had from a couple years ago, and there's no problem using it on my desktop machine rather than my laptop.
text_fidelity_b: Seagate 600 SSD 480 GB SATA 6 Gb/s 2.5-Inch 7mm Z-Height Solid State Drive ST480HM000

First of all, it is huge! Second, it comes with a 10-inch tabletop or floor level light ring with its own stand. Of course, there are the two remotes and an app you can use to take photos and set your light levels with.

I'm an amateur at using ring lights for my photo taking, and this one is no piece of cake to set up. The instructions are terrible for someone who is usually pretty good at following them. and the remote and app take some playing around with to figure them out. Also, the remote does not automatically pair with your phone the next time you want to use it, so you have to pair them over again. This is a bit annoying.

I have a Note 10+ with a case and it barely fits into the holder. I'm so glad it does. The whole setup feels nice and sturdy all the way around, from the bottom of the stand to phone holders. I sell bulk bought makeup online, and it's nice to have a ring big enough that it doesn't show up on the surface of the shiny palettes. I can place it so there are no shadows or bright spots, and the light is up far enough that it is not in my way. It is that big. I am working with four to six inch items, so that helps, too. It makes my life so much easier.

The ten inch ring light is great for getting perfect shoe photos. I love buying shoes, and always take photos to put on the end of the boxes, so I can see exactly what I have at a glance. It makes picking out my shoes for the day easy, when I can see the actual shoe, and not a drawing of it.

These lights are the best I've bought. They are made very well, and so is everything they come with. You will not find a better setup at a better cost. A beginner or novice will have everything you need to start taking photos or videos right out of the box. You may, however, find better instructions on how to put a setup together in a different set, but then you wouldn't get half the amount or half the quality of the items you get in this one. It may take some trial and error, but if I can figure out how to set this up, I'm pretty sure anyone can. I have cognitive difficulties and things don't come easy. It took me a good while and I did ask for some help with one thing from my son, but I got it done, and it was worth the trouble. 4 stars ✨

It's metal, not plastic, and has a nice heft and feels durable. It looks great. And audio quality is very good. It comes with a micro SD card already installed and ready to go. It also comes with a set of ear buds, a lavalier microphone which can be used instead of the built-in mics, a cord for line-in recording, and a USB charging cord. No charger is included. And it does not come with a protective pouch or sleeve. But it is boxed nicely.

It records in user-selectable WAV or MP3 formats in various selectable bitrates. It has adjustable gain control and a noise reduction function. One important function for voice recording is the ability to monitor while recording using ear buds or headphones, and this recorder has that capability. The display screen isn't as sharp and clear as it is portrayed in the listing photos, but it is decent.

Now for the minor negatives, for which I dinged a star off the review rating. One is the printing labeling the buttons on the one I received is only a little lighter than the color of the recorder, making them very hard to read. That means you have to memorize the button location and functions or keep the user manual handy for reference. And that leads to the second negative, and that is the print in the user manual is tiny. Really tiny. I looked for a PDF version online and couldn't find one. The manual suggests visiting the brand's web site, but neither the manual nor the box provide a URL. Or even the listing brand name (Tenmatec) for that matter. I wound taking photographs of the manual pages with a tablet so I could enlarge them for easier reading. The other minor negative is that it has no USB-C port, only a micro USB for recharging or connecting to a computer for moving files around.

Other than that it's a good recorder. It has one-button functionality (although there is a slight delay when starting a recording while it starts up). Because of its metal construction and heft it feels good in-hand and looks really good.
text_fidelity_b: TenmaTec Voice Recorder with Playback,80GB Voice Activated Recorder with DSP Noise Reduction,Dual Microphones, Mp3,Speaker,Password Protect,for Music,Overdubbing,Studio,Dictation,Interview

text_fidelity_a:
PIONEER Hi-Res Audio in-Ear Headphones, Black SE-CH3T(B) I own several pairs of earbuds. I just seem to accumulate them like I do my reading glasses -- several pairs in each room where I tend to use them. Most of mine are in the price range $20-30, so those are the ones I'm using for comparison. Based on that, these new Pioneer earbuds seem to be the best of that group.

I listen mostly to classical music with a smattering of other genres (folk, 1960s-70s rock, Broadway). These provided acceptable performance for all genres, but do seem to lack some low-end bass response. One of my test recordings is the Erich Kunzel/Cincinnati Symphony recording of Tchaikovsky's "1812 Overture" with cannons, and the low-end loss was noticeable. Still, the rest of the sound is excellent, and these will work just fine for my day-to-day listening -- music that I have going on in the background while working on something else. For serious listening, I'll use my over-the-ear headphones.

Good performance for the price. I like these.
text_fidelity_b: PIONEER Hi-Res Audio in-Ear Headphones, Black SE-CH3T(B)

text_fidelity_a:
Securifi Almond - (3 Minute Setup) Touchscreen Wireless Router/Range Extender The tech geek in our household kept telling me there was nothing we could do to improve on the truly horrendous wireless internet service we have. He said we were stuck with the ISP we have and with their router (which he has in the far back bedroom, on the other side of our apartment from the pricey smart TV I haven't been able to use for anything but watching cable news). I haven't been able to stream anything from Amazon Prime, nor can I access the internet at all through the TV. So in complete frustration, without telling him, I ordered the Securifi Almond. Price was one factor in my decision, but I knew I wasn't going to be able to depend on him to help me set anything up and I'm not all that tech savvy.

One of the attractive selling points of this router is that it can be used either as a router or as a range extender. I planned to set it up as a range extender to see if I could get a better signal near my TV, but also had in mind that I might be able to persuade a certain somebody to try it as our router in place of the one that I feel like is defective (or just crummy) from our ISP.

I set it up myself. I just followed the installation on screen, and it was a snap. Fortunately, I knew what our log-in info was for our network so I didn't have to ask for help. I wasn't sure how it was supposed to work with the ethernet cable, so I plugged the Almond into the LAN port of of my TV and into one of the ports with a TV icon on the router. Then I tested it. Wow. The streaming is so much better than it was that I signed up for Netflix and started binging on "House of Cards." I still have the rotating download timer come up once or twice during an episode, but it gets done pretty quickly and the episode finishes playing. Before, I couldn't even load an episode or, worse, it would play a minute then completely drop the connection to the internet.

So I'm quite happy. This is a sleek little baby that works. I can see at a glance that I'm connected, which is reassuring. I haven't yet tried it in its router mode, but as a range extender it works great. You need to use the little stowaway stylus that comes with it when you're selecting onscreen functions, but as long as you remember to re-stow it, you've always got it handy if you need it.
text_fidelity_b: Securifi Almond - (3 Minute Setup) Touchscreen Wireless Router/Range Extender

text_fidelity_a:
Jiusion Telescope Eyepiece Plossl Eyepiece 32mm with 1.25inch Filter Threaded, Astronomical Telescope Lens 50% FOV increase at this price? This is the lowest priced Plössl I've ever seen and the reason for choosing it. Curiosity.

As a physicist with a too time-consuming career to fool around with optical Garage-a-Tronics projects, it's time for fun. After >40 years, I'd guess 1/3 of my time was in electro-optical systems. My responsibilities included one of the nation's most sophisticated optical design, fabrication, and 50-200 layers of Å thickness vapor deposition coating capability (200 layers is no limit … simply the most I've seen engineered)

You have to give them credit. Chinese optics are extraordinary and have been for 20 years. Asian pricing has wholly changed the marketplace. The crazy low prices have made complex systems affordable to the mass market. Optical grinding facilities remaining in the US are confined to a handful of custom, proto-typing houses run by old-timers with a decidedly different product application than consumer use.

The Plössl eyepiece is quite expensive to manufacture given the nature of the glass, coatings, and its precisely coordinated concave and convex lenses to neutralize internal reflections.

The Plössl has tradeoffs. All optical systems do. For example, Plössl's increased FOV comes with an eye relief confined to 70–80% of focal length.

Lenses are analog. Performance is not binary. 'Lowest price' in optics might be misunderstood. Optics lots begin production targeted at a spec performance that makes a profit. A production lot will yield a normal distribution to spec. On the upper end of the distribution are a few 'blue diamonds' commanding a super premium. Theoretically, 66%, will meet the target spec. Production lots begin life as profitable, spec-centered customers. 7% would be expected to fall short of some spec performance (i.e. start 107% of what you need) … Harvard MBA's demanding perfection in all things except stock value have never come to terms with normal analog distributions in scientific endeavors.

The lenses come without ref to detail specs, so I would believe the factory is emptying the shelves of sub-spec product here. Spec fallout, in my experience, may have little or nothing to do with operator perceptions of performance.

Excellent fun.

Was my review helpful? If so, click "Helpful" so I can know. Trying hard to put integrity into reviews
text_fidelity_b: Jiusion Telescope Eyepiece Plossl Eyepiece 32mm with 1.25inch Filter Threaded, Astronomical Telescope Lens

text_fidelity_a:
TP-Link AC1200 Reliable Dual Band WiFi Router (Archer C50) Update, Aug 2016: It's been 5 months since I installed this router and it has the distinction of never needing to be rebooted yet! That's a record for me, since some of my past routers needed a reboot every week or two (or even every day or two). I continue to be impressed with the rock-solid performance of this TP-LINK. It's not fancy and lacks some high-end features, but I'll take solid, dependable performance over flash any day.

Original review:
While this router won’t satisfy the needs of those who have complex networking requirements or those who like to tinker and tweak, it offers solid performance, AC speeds and good coverage at a very reasonable price point. If you’re looking to go to AC speed but don’t want all the bells and whistles, this offers a lot for the money.

The footprint is very small compared with other routers I have, which is a nice change. The overall build quality seems very good, and the two antennae are firmly attached (another problem I’ve had with lower-end routers). It has an off switch which is handy if you need to do a reboot. It runs warm but not hot.

Setup is very straightforward if you want to keep the default settings. Basically just plug it into a PC, access the router menu with your browser, set the network name and password, and you’re done. You can access more advanced features if needed, but for a basic setup the time required is less than 5 minutes.

Performance has been impressive. I also have AC routers from D-Link and Linksys that are far more costly than this, but this little guy holds his own when it comes to coverage and throughput. For example, I get Internet connection speeds of about 62mBps with my D-Link DIR-880L. This router, with the same PC and network card, gives me 50mBps. Wireless coverage is a little more spotty with this router on fringe areas (e.g., for a PC located a floor above and at the opposite end of the house from the router) but it still maintains a connection, albeit at lower speeds.

This does lack some features that could be helpful for some situations. It has a USB port, but only has one, and it’s a 2.0 USB port. It lacks a gigabit port as well. But again, for the price, it offers a lot of performance. So far I’ve had zero problems or glitches.

This router won’t excite a power user or satisfy complex networking requirements/demands, but for the basics, it gets the job done with solid speed and performance. Well worth considering if you’re looking for an inexpensive router.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link AC1200 Reliable Dual Band WiFi Router (Archer C50)

SanDisk Ultra Fit 128GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive - SDCZ43-128G-GAM46 It just landed in the return envelope today... There has been three major things that led to this:
1) The Vault software stopped responding and started crashing every time I tried to run it. Data inside it were obviously inaccessible. So...
2) I decided to make it brand new and reformat the drive. Using just Windows explorer it did not work (refused), then using disk management - no success, finally using prompt and unconditional formatting (both full and quick) would end up in reporting that disk is not accessible - apparently there is writing protection on it that I could not get passed and it would not allow me to reformat it. So...
3) After attempting to reformat the disk became unreadable and Windows could not see it (disk management would see it as raw partition, not able to format it). Next, I took it off the USB port in order to reinsert it and then I almost burned my finger! This thing was so HOT I could fry an egg on it, if it was bigger! After reinserting into the USB port it would still be unrecognizable.
In short, the disk became a small brick and landed in the return envelope.
Avoid SanDisk as they apparently shovel the write protection down your throat and you can't do anything with your drive later on. So much for your customer flexibility with your product. Rather pick a very similar, ultra-small Samsung USB drive of the same size, also available from Amazon. That one comes clean (i.e. no imposed software nor writing protection) and apparently does not heat at all, or very little compared to this little oven.

Fitbit One Wireless Activity Plus Sleep Tracker, Black Three things have changed my life! FITBIT, Walking Workouts and Walking 4 Fun.

FITBIT ONE - I have been faithfully wearing it. Using the calories in and out featured on the app. It has a safety leash and I wear it attached to my bra. I do a Jessica Smith DVD - 10K Walking Workout (see link on bottom of this review) and Leslie Sansone ("Walk at Home"). However, ONE is super accurate on my walks outside and around the office. My bottom line is 10K steps a day but I tend to walk 17K a day. I worked my way up to this since October 2015. I have a sedentary job so walking happens 3 to 4 times a day with a minimum of a mile on each walk. Yes, I have lost weight, @ 40 lbs. There is at least that much more that needs to be lost as well. Hair color is silver if that helps you define the situation.

I love the little activity record feature and use it often (hold down the button to start and hold it down to end when activity is over). This is great when competing with friends where a challenge is inevitable. Speaking of friends. YEAH! That is where the FITBITs excel. I have a few friends in my community now and I love keeping up with them. Motivation features are fantastic!

This little baby doesn't buzz, which also means that the battery life is HUGE!! I think it goes 7 to 8 days before I need to be charged up. I tend to let it go dead because it warns you it needs to be charged about 1 1/2 days before it really does. I've only charged mine 3x now. It takes about an hour to charge. I wait until the visible battery = FULL!

This sweet little tracker is awesome! I started test driving the flex before getting the ONE which I also enjoyed but not as much as this one. I will buy the HR when this ONE dies or I just feel like bringing home another one. The reason I like this one better than the flex is because I don't tend to be an arm swinger and for me this one seems to work better (walking while pushing a cart). The best thing about the arm band models is that you affix it and forget it (until charging time) for which you should get a phone alert.

I don't bother with the sleep feature because I have an app (Sleep Cycle Alarm) on the phone that I use for which I love the beautiful melodious wake up sound. However the ONE comes with a little band for you to slide the ONE into obtain the reading for sleep.

text_fidelity_a:
Anker Soundcore Bluetooth Speaker with 24-Hour Playtime, 66-Feet Bluetooth Range & Built-in Mic, Dual-Driver Portable Wireless Speaker with Low Harmonic Distortion and Superior Sound - Blue I own the A3143 Premium Stereo Bluetooth speaker (2x10W=20W) which sounds great, but it doesn't have a microphone or the longer battery life of this lower-cost A3102 SoundCore speaker (2x3W=6W). The features and sound characteristics are different, but which is the better choice depends on personal preference. To me based on sound quality alone, the A3143 wins hands down. The bass is stronger (more power is required to drive the lower frequencies than the higher frequencies), but I also find overall frequency response to be more balanced and accurate for instruments and vocals. For either speaker, I'd recommend using an EQ app to set the frequency response and spatial effects to your preference (I use Bass EQ from Coocent). Interestingly, the maximum volume level for both the A3143 and this A3102 SoundCore are about the same.

The A3102 has a brighter sound overall. The A3102 is good as a general purpose speaker, and it is excellent to use with a cell phone. The A3102 microphone (which the A3143 doesn't have) and speaker quality for voice calling are crisp and clear. My dad who can't hear very well often could not understand me on my cell phone handset or its speakerphone, but had no problem when I used the A3102.

So for long battery life, good overall music speaker, and particularly for use as a microphone/speakerphone for voice calls, A3102 is a good choice. For best music reproduction, the A3143. For either, Anker's quality and customer support are among the best in the industry.
text_fidelity_b: Anker Soundcore Bluetooth Speaker with 24-Hour Playtime, 66-Feet Bluetooth Range & Built-in Mic, Dual-Driver Portable Wireless Speaker with Low Harmonic Distortion and Superior Sound - Blue

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Tap - Alexa-Enabled Portable Bluetooth Speaker I find the skill set/setup dubious and the Alexa app was slow and very glitchy. This review is strictly about the device as a streaming Wi/Fi/Bluetooth speaker and sound quality.

I am an Amazon Prime customer and all my music is on Amazon streaming. Both ease of use (on Amazon Music/Pandora, etc. only) and sound in one word, Superb! I'm completely surprised because I own the $200+ UEBoom (which has been sitting unused on a shelf, I had to go look for it) and assumed the sound on that would be much superior as reviews and it's reputation suggest. Not so! I just listened back to back.

Without intending to compare them, I got my UEBoom to play while I setup the marvelous SOAIY Aurora projector (upgraded version), and in the back of my mind notice the music, not played very loudly because it's nighttime, was rather muddy; I think it wows people for its volume and base. On a whim I switched to my new Amazon Tap received today (I hadn't much time to experiment with it) and... Wow! Fantastic sound quality! Much more enjoyable than the popular UEBoom.

Better flat frequency response like a pair of reference headphones (like the Sony Studio MV6 I prefer), more clear definition and detail, not muddy, better treble response (I don't mean tinny or lack of bass), and bass rivaling that of UEBoom. Oh, the main thing I noticed also, which confused me at first, is the wide stereo dispersion (?), um, I mean wide field effect and stereo separation. I literally looked at the cylinder puzzled as to what I was hearing and mentally verifying only this device was on and was the source of the sound I was hearing.

The UEBoom always sounded merely monaural from one sourcepoint; this sounded like surround sound effect applied to a two-speaker (not 5.1+) tv. I was amazed at what my senses were reporting to me. Okay, I'm going to say it, to my ears, and I have a class D amplifier and 5 pairs of quality headphones of different brands, the sound of this Amazon Tap is superior, right out of the box. I was amazed. And of course streaming directly sans device is certainly more convenient. It "just works". (After connecting to your Wi-Fi network.)

I learned to say "playlist rock", since I have a playlist named rock, or it will play all my Amazon music in the genre "rock". I did ask for the weather after entering my zip code through the Alexa app, which I dislike, and it responded with detailed information. Luckily music playback works directly without a need for app use. I will now mention this superior sound quality is half the price of it's aforementioned similar-sized competitor. I'm now really glad I bought it :)
***
Update: I returned it. It couldn't find a track in my music library, I checked title of track and found it instantly on my Fire, but the Tap still couldn't find it; everything I've tried to do with it either completely fails, or I resort to a different device because it's quicker and more convenient. It's mistaken "no" for "yes" and when asking for Julie Andrews started playing the soundtrack to Fifty Shades of Gray. It's been sitting on the kitchen counter unused. I could spend the money elsewhere better (I purchased two Fire HD 6" tablets which are excellent, speedy devices and fit into my front pocket). To each their own.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Tap - Alexa-Enabled Portable Bluetooth Speaker

Blink Outdoor Camera Wall Mount Bracket, Hard Protective Case and Metal Mount for Blink XT2 Cameras Weather Proof Adjustable Indoor Outdoor Mount and Cover for Blink Home Security(3 Pack, Black) When I installed my Blink XT2, I found I needed to move it a little lower so I could maybe see the face of the delivery person. Thinking I could unscrew the mount without removing the camera, I turned the camera to one side so I could access the screws. The camera fell to the floor. A little bit of friction is not sufficient to hold these cameras. That is when I started looking at these mounts which SHOULD be included in the box.

This is in several parts. Plastic camera-enclosing parts are held together with 4 small screws. The metal part is attached to the wall with 3 flat-head #6 screws.

Unscrew the adjusting part so the base of the mount can be attached to the wall. Do not try to adjust the angle unless this part is loose. Use care when tightening the screws - do it manually so the screws are not over-tightened. The aluminum base could be cracked by over-tightening.

The small screws that are used to attach the back cover to the front should be machine screws, and the posts into which they are screwed should be metal. This is my opinion and is because these screws will have to be removed and reinstalled every time the batteries are replaced.

One piece of plastic had a small 'tab' on it that had to be cut off before the back cover would attach to the front.

A hole in the bottom of the plastic is there to allow a charging cable to be attached. If you do not plan to use rechargeable batteries and have no need for the USB cable, plug the hole so insects do not go inside looking for a new home. I used a small piece of closed cell foam packing material (photo).

If you want to use these mounts with the earlier Blink cameras, you might want to use some foam so the camera does not move around inside the enclosure (photo).
text_fidelity_b: Blink Outdoor Camera Wall Mount Bracket, Hard Protective Case and Metal Mount for Blink XT2 Cameras Weather Proof Adjustable Indoor Outdoor Mount and Cover for Blink Home Security(3 Pack, Black)

Bone Conduction Headphones with Noise Cancelling MIC for Clear Calls, IPX6 Waterproof Open-Ear Bluetooth Wireless Headset for Calling, Running, Bicycling, Hiking (Green) Bone conduction headphones have become quite popular and because of this, there are many to choose from. This specific model is quite minimalist. A thin metal frame with the vibration units and electronics hanging off it.

In terms of comfort, there is no adjustability to the metal frame so it may take some getting used to because the frame may feel like they are too big or too small depending on your head size. For me it felt a little bit loose but I came to realize that it actually stayed where you place it and it really wasn't a problem.

For sound quality, this bone conduction headphone will never match a nice pair of over-ear headphones but that really isn't what it's for. By leaving the ears open, one is still able to stay aware of the surroundings, making it great for cycling and jogging where hearing the traffic is essential for safety reasons.

A pair of earplugs are included with this product and with one or both in, one can really appreciate the difference between regular headphones and bone conduction. You can still hear the music (or in my case, audiobook) through the earplugs because of the bone vibration but all outside sound is cut off. This means that you'd be able to listen to music over the sound of a loud machine.

I have tried a few different pairs of bone conduction headphones and these are the ones that I have stuck with so far. The buttons maybe be somewhat limited (just two buttons that control volume and power), but they are easily reachable and not hard to press and the IPX6 means it's water resistant against rain and sweat.
text_fidelity_b: Bone Conduction Headphones with Noise Cancelling MIC for Clear Calls, IPX6 Waterproof Open-Ear Bluetooth Wireless Headset for Calling, Running, Bicycling, Hiking (Green)

text_fidelity_a:
Zinwell ZAT-970A Digital to Analog TV Converter Box (for Antenna Use) We needed to save some money, and I'd heard that Over The Air broadcasts included channels you wouldn't otherwise get. My Dish TV account provided local channels and a whole bunch of channels I didn't use; but the OTA feature really helps!

I paired the Zinwell digital / analog converter box (highly rated, outstanding Amazon price) with the Radio Shack Antennacraft® HDX1000 Amplified HDTV Antenna (also highly rated). You should know one thing -- the mast size for the Dish TV is larger than the mast size for the Antennacraft antenna, so you can't just remove the Dish and replace it with the Antennacraft on the same mast. But it is an easy install.

As a trial, before going up to the roof (2 story house), I set the Antennacraft in the downstairs window that has a view to the southwest (the direction our local TV stations broadcast from). Without the Zinwell, you're limited to the low power analog stations (mostly Spanish language, a few home shopping stations). I think I got about 6 stations. Then I plugged in the Zinwell in line between the antenna and the TV (after disconnecting the Dish TV feed), did a scan, and had 20 channels. Repeated the process upstairs (remember, we have a 2 story) and had 22 channels!! All the local tv stations (NBC, ABC, CW, ION, PBS, etc.) that broadcast digitally came through great!! Unfortunately, it started raining :( so after the rain stopped, I only got as far as getting the mast installed outdoors before it got too dark. It won't take long to finish.

Only one Zinwell related item: You're supposed to be able to choose the feed from the Zinwell to the TV to be either Coax or the Composite (yellow video, red and white audio). I couldn't get the composite to work in setup, but the coax worked just fine. Haven't had a chance to see if, once programmed, the composite would work, or if for some reason I hooked it up to my tv incorrectly (hard to imagine), but ... since the coax works so well, and video and audio quality are great, I'm money ahead and not complaining!!

So when do I break even? $80 antenna plus 2 $40 boxes = $160; Dish TV was costing me about $55/month (yeah, once you've been a subscriber for a while, there's essentially no customer retention policy, so, good by Dish!! -- and that's probably true for Directv and Comcast, too). So after 3 months, essentially at the start of January, I'm home free!! Thanks, Amazon, you're helping me save money, and that's really great!!

NOTE: I only ordered one Zinwell to test out things, now I've ordered a second for our other TV (didn't want to put too much at risk if it didn't work, but it works great!).

NOTE 2: The gov't coupon program is long dead, no hope of getting $40 off on one, just be glad if you waited that these things are as reasonably priced as they are.
text_fidelity_b: Zinwell ZAT-970A Digital to Analog TV Converter Box (for Antenna Use)

text_fidelity_a:
SAMSUNG (MB-ME32GA/AM) 32GB 95MB/s (U1) microSDHC EVO Select Memory Card with Full-Size Adapter So far so good on this micro sD card.

This is the third micro sD card I’ve bought for my phones since October 2015.

The other two were the 32GB EVO Class 10 Micro SDHC up to 48MB/s with Adapter (MB-MP32DA/AM). And, I was definitely elated to see those were no longer available. Sorry that it is mean-spirited, but after knowing why – I think anyone would be happy to see a fault product go away.

Why did I choose this one?

I purchased the 32GB EVO Class 10 Micro SDHC up to 48MB/s with Adapter (MB-MP32DA/AM) in October of 2015 for my Samsung GS4, and only two (2) months later – I needed a brand new one. Why? It failed. No warning, nothing. Just a failure. The phone wasn’t dropped, shocked, or smashed. It had NO water damage either.

And this wouldn’t be the first failure either for that particular model.

The sD card I bought in December failed as well, but I’ll give it up for it – It went OVER three (3) years before failing. It failed April 3, 2019. I remember that because of the event it failed during. I would’ve expected the failure when I transferred the sD card from the S4 to the S8 in May 2018, but the card still worked.

There were no signs of pending failure or issues. The night before (4/2), it worked and I was able to retrieve some photos off of it.

My mother and I went to Knott’s Berry Farm for the Boysenberry Festival. And, any photos take before we left – GONE. No error messages – just gone. I didn’t know until I got home.

What photos I have were the return photos from the drive home. I had briefly glanced at the card data (on my phone) at about 2pm, but after that (without being dropped, banged, over-heated) the card failed. I know some will ask why I didn’t back them up – I was in transit, driving on the freeway, so it wasn’t feasible.

All I know is that my photos were gone. Again, the phone wasn’t dropped, smashed, shocked. Also, no water damage.

So, I had to purchase another sD card for my phone. This time I chose this one – Samsung 32GB 95MB/s (U1) MicroSD EVO Select Memory Card with Adapter (MB-ME32GA/AM).

From April 2019 to the date of this review, it’s been pretty solid. Though I’m not taking any chances. I also store photos to my S8’s internal storage as well as the sD card.

As far as recommending this one – so far it’s working and has been for over five (5) months, so I’ll recommend it for now.

I’ll update the review if things change.
text_fidelity_b: SAMSUNG (MB-ME32GA/AM) 32GB 95MB/s (U1) microSDHC EVO Select Memory Card with Full-Size Adapter

text_fidelity_a:
Rosewill 3.5 Inch Hard Drive Enclosure to USB 3.0 / eSATA. External Hard Drive Case Aluminum Body, Built-in Cooling Fan and Fan Switch. Support 3.5” SATA III / II / I Hard Drive up to 6TB and UASP function. Wouldn't recognize on the eSATA port. It would detect the HDD, but would not format nor store data. I thought it would be plug and play. I submitted a return request (which the seller approved), but after extensive Googling, discovered how to make it work on my machine.

1) For Windows 7 (I think Windows 10 may not have this issue), make sure you have the registry entry to allow AHCI.
2) In BIOS, make sure your boot devices are in proper order.
3) In BIOS, update RAID configuration to AHCI.

After that, it is operating as expected.
text_fidelity_b: Rosewill 3.5 Inch Hard Drive Enclosure to USB 3.0 / eSATA. External Hard Drive Case Aluminum Body, Built-in Cooling Fan and Fan Switch. Support 3.5” SATA III / II / I Hard Drive up to 6TB and UASP function.

Belkin Grip Candy Sheer Case for iPhone 5 and 5S (Purple and Turquoise) This is the second case I have gotten that I could not give a good rating because of the bottom part, which does not fit with the adapter (to allow older devices to work with the new iPhone), and it does not fit most professional cables that go into the headphone jack.
Because my car has a built-in charger and system that plays with i-technology (previous generations), I HAVE to use the adapter, not just the new wire. Because I am a dancer and instructor and use my phone for job every day, I HAVE to have a case that lets me plug into our system. For those reasons, this case, like the last one I got, is useless to me.

Could you peel back the case to leave the bottom exposed? Yes. But over time, this warps the plastic and creates a loose fit, and putting it on and taking if off can cause the screen protector to come off around the edges.

Could you cut part of the bottom to allow the adapter and wires to fit? No. The plastic is thick enough that the wire will still not fit the headphone jack. As for the adapter, it might fit, but it will want to come out because the thickness, again, will make it want to separate.

So far, the only case to fit my iPhone is a pretty cheap import that has very thin plastic and is generally not a great case either. Is it a design problem with the phone as well? Maybe, but the people making cases should take that into account and design something that works with the iPhone 5 as it is, not as we wish it were. I guess I'm keeping my brand X case a bit longer.
text_fidelity_b: Belkin Grip Candy Sheer Case for iPhone 5 and 5S (Purple and Turquoise)

Of course, I would never believe them without double-checking for myself, and I found out it was indeed an outright lie. Even the oldest DOCSIS versions can handle more than my 30Mbps connection. I suppose the lie was because they want me to rent their modem for $10 or more a month and relinquish control of my own network to them.

That said, it makes sense to upgrade when convenient to be sure you're future proofed. Eventually even the cheapest Internet plans will be upgraded to higher speeds. When I heard that I could register this on Comcast's network online without having to call them (and have them speak extremely condescendingly to me even though I'm a Systems Engineer), I was sold. Worth doing.

Note that just because DOCSIS 3.0 can reach speeds of 10Gbps with maxed out number of channels, this modem is 680Mbps, which will be out of date eventually, when we finally get Gigabit Ethernet to residences.

Another (of a million) thing(s) I hate about Comcast is that they by default use your AP (that they rent to you as part of a router/AP/modem combo) to create a public (virtual) wireless AP for their other customers. They say this will not affect your bandwidth, but it can affect your throughput. And it uses your electricity. And why would you want to help Comcast, when they take advantage of you any chance they can.

Point of all this is me encouraging you to get your own modem, get your own router and AP (or combo unit, although I prefer them separate) and pare down your ISP bill as much as you can. Stop giving them money.

Note that apparently if you get voice service through Comcast, you'll still need their combo modem unit of some sort. Well, cut that service from your monthly budget too. If we just had some competition, I'd cut Comcast out of my life completely.

Another thing is that if you have their modem and you need help with it, they may call it your responsibility and charge you for any "help" they provide. At least if you own your own stuff, you'll know if it's your problem or theirs.

Modem is straightforward and easy to use as any. If you ever download at high rates for days on end, it'll need cycled, but that's not the modem's fault; it just happens.
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR Cable Modem CM500 - Compatible with all Cable Providers incl. Xfinity, Spectrum, Cox | For Cable Plans up to 400Mbps | DOCSIS 3.0

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Chromebook 15 CB3-532-C4ZZ, Celeron N3060, 15.6" HD, 4GB LPDDR3, 32GB Storage, Google Chrome Electronics are a fact of life and most families have multiple electronic devices to get through their day. My family of four has four cell phones, about six different pcs, laptops, and tablets, and three printers. Now, we also have our first ever Chromebook thanks to this Amazon product.

Chromebooks, I quickly learned, differ from the usual windows or apple laptop in several important ways and chief among them is the limit on the number of things you can download. If you have specific games and other things you want to download, they may not work. I already knew this going in but I can tell from reading other reviews that some people were not aware that it worked this way and they now have a device with limited usefulness.

Once you accept the Acer Chromebook for what it is, you will find that it does serve as a handy device. It’s excellent for browsing the internet, creating google docs, using google apps, and pretty much doing all things google. I am already a google chrome user when I go online and I already use many apps from the google play, so what this Chromebook offers is compatible with my needs.

Looking at other specifics of this Acer Chromebook, it is about the same size as my old laptop, at least in terms of the screen size. The image is good, although I have seen other laptops/tablets with more pixels and sharper images. Still, it should be sufficient for most needs, and it has a good deal to offer for the price. I have noticed that the charge doesn’t hold as long as the manufacturer claims and the bottom of the Chromebook does feel hot a little sooner than with others. But the Acer Chromebook is still functional and it performs well enough for my needs.

Electronics are a fact of life and as much as we try to limit their use, they are here to stay. Since we have to have them and use them, it makes sense to get the electronics that best suit our needs for a fair price and this Acer Chromebook does exactly that. It does have its limits and it cannot do everything that a windows or apple laptop can do, but as long as you know the limitations before you purchase, you should be fine.

I'm training for my first half marathon and wanted something that could track my distance and time, as well as my heart rate...but at the same time I needed it to be very simple. This watch had great reviews across the board.
Each day you run the watch has to reset position (unless you just wear it throughout the day). Do not hit the GPS button until you are outside and clear of your home/building. A couple of times I tried to get a jump start on the watch and hit the button while getting ready inside. My run was off by nearly 200 feet. This may not seem like a lot but when you are running multiple miles it adds up.
As long as you hit the GPS button while outside though you won't have any problems. It was dead on every time when I did this.
The battery life lasts (depending on your distance) about four days with consistent use.
It recharges very quickly so if you run in the morning and at night, you will easily have a full charge prior to your second run...typically takes 3 hours or so for a full charge from completely dead.
Definitely recommend the watch, especially for beginner and intermediate runners.

text_fidelity_a:
ELECJET MagJet, Magnetic USB C Charger Adapter, 4.3A 87W Fast Charge, 6 Pin Reversible, QC 3.0 & PD, for New MacBook Pro/Air and Any USB C Devices (White) So far, very impressive. The magnetic breakaway connector is tiny, and its 87W-capable cable is lightweight and flexible-- way more so than the Apple USB-C charging cable that came with my 15" MacBook Pro and its 87W charger. It looks good, fully Apple-class in design and construction. But what sets this apart is a clever technical detail:

It uses a six-pin design approach that splits the charging current between two pairs of pins at the corners of the pin array, cutting the current through each by half. That is clever and I think unique, and it should make life easier on the port and probably on the Mac by reducing arcing and generally providing a better, more robust connection.

The magnet is nice and strong, and the L-shaped cable configuration lowers the torque on the connector, reducing unwanted disconnects while ensuring it breaks away when you want it to.

As with most USB-C charging cables and magnetic-breakaway adaptors, this is for charging only-- no data will traverse it. If you want a MagSafe-like adaptor that will handle both 87W charging and high-speed data, check out the Snapnator, also available here on Amazon. I have one of those too, and it's excellent, but it sticks straight out from the Mac and is more prone to disconnects, partly because I use it with the Apple charging cable that is so puzzlingly heavy and stiff.

My only issue with the design of this cable is that its strain relief construction is identical to Apple's, meaning the cable will eventually wear at the edge of the strain-relief. That's a common issue with charging cables and something we've all come to live with but it's still regrettable. I do wish cable designers would pay better attention to it, but it's universal, even with Apple's premium-priced cables.

The cable came in a nice little zipper case made of some sort of rigid formed fabric covered with a rubbery coating. Unfortunately there was a paper bar-code sticker on the case, and when I peeled it off, off came the coating. Ah well.

I'll post any updates over time.
text_fidelity_b: ELECJET MagJet, Magnetic USB C Charger Adapter, 4.3A 87W Fast Charge, 6 Pin Reversible, QC 3.0 & PD, for New MacBook Pro/Air and Any USB C Devices (White)

text_fidelity_a:
JVC Wireless Noise Canceling Over Ear Headphones, Bluetooth, Instant paring with NFC Technology - HAS90BNB, Black, One Size My experience with JVC up to this point has been with video equipment and televisions. My experiences have been positive so I hoped that this would be a good set of Active Noise Canceling (ANC) phones. I have worked with a lot of ANC phones – Bose, Sennheiser, Sony, Philips and more. Almost every set I have used has had some flaw, either in the ANC or in the sound profile. These JVC phones are interesting in that regard. The sound profile is nearly spot on, but the ANC is on the conservative side.

I’ll go over the ANC first. This is not a real competitor for the high end Sony or Bose sets and if the main thing you want from a set of ANC phones is noise elimination then these are far from the strongest or most aggressive. I have a fan that I use as the main test for ANC phones, and with the most aggressive phones the fan is almost completely wiped out. The JVC phones do cancel a good bit of noise, but it leaves a good bit of sound behind that Bose in particular eliminates. Now, that said, ANC headphones that can cancel more than these are almost universally much more expensive, often by double the price. These are what can probably be called “good enough for most”. For me, I like a more aggressive headphone, but these cancel enough ambient noise that when I am listening to music I don’t hear much else.

Many ANC phones fiddle with the sound profile to compensate for some of the lost frequency response, usually in the bass range and at the expense of the midrange. These phones are very unusual in that they don’t really seem to impact the sound profile much at all. And, the sound is very balanced. The bass is good, not overdriven (if you have ever used Dre Beats or Monster phones, you know exactly what I’m talking about). The midrange is warm and music sounds like it has the right depth as a result. The highs are clear and vocals sound very clean. The sound profile does not seem to be different between when the ANC function is on or off, though turning on the ANC does enhance the volume (which you can observe by having the headphones off when you activate the ANC in the middle of playback.

The ear cups are comfortable and I can wear these for a while before I need to take them off for comfort reasons. They don’t seem to get too warm when wearing for a while which is good. They’re not the most comfortable phones I have used, but they are better than many.

They connect via Bluetooth and I had no issues pairing and connecting them to my phone.

My favorite feature is that there is an independent volume control on the headphones themselves that does not change the volume setting on the source device. This is a feature that is a bit unusual; often, when the phones have a volume control on them it impacts the system volume when adjusted.

So, there is one thing about these phones that I think needs some improvement. Included with them is a cloth bag for protection, and that’s just not going to cut it, particularly in this price range. A bag prevents the contents from getting dirty but provides no damage protection. For the asking price (presently $149) these should have a hard case that at a minimum provides crush resistance.

I am very pleased with these headphones, more than I expected to be. They sound great, though the ANC is passable. My biggest issue isn’t with the phones themselves but with the lack of a suitable protective case. Hopefully JVC will resolve that issue in the near future. If you want a good set of ANC phones without spending north of $300, these are worth a look.
text_fidelity_b: JVC Wireless Noise Canceling Over Ear Headphones, Bluetooth, Instant paring with NFC Technology - HAS90BNB, Black, One Size

TRENDnet Wireless AC1750 Dual Band Gigabit Router with USB 3.0 Share Port, Pre-Encrypted, TEW-812DRU Let me preface this review by explaining that I work in the IT industry and support a variety of businesses with enough thorough experience in networking to say with certainty - the router I received is absolute garbage.

Now, normally I'd say for this price that you should set you expectations quite low - being in the field I'm in, I understand that almost all consumer routers are not great options, and the ones that are somewhat viable are on the $300+ range. Not everybody has the money or cares enough to invest this much - I get that.

So, that leaves me and my old roommate pretty much one option; the TRENDnet Wireless AC1750. He doesn't need much and especially doesn't want to spend much, it was tough getting him to go high enough in price to even this router- the old router he had came with his cable subscription 3 years ago. It worked fine but was sometimes slow with downloading over WiFi, not surprising. From the research and reviews, and most importantly the price - we decided to try this Trendnet AC1750 router.

WOW what garbage - he no longer gets WiFi in his bathroom corner of the house - it is a VERY small 2 bedroom apartment. How in the world can this router not handle a signal from 20 feet away, with only 2 walls in between? A router of this caliber (even at this price) should EASILY be able to handle covering a 2 bedroom small apartment. Period.

On to the second problem - even if we're connected, the WiFi signal drops constantly, I have to now reset this router every single day by unplugging it and plugging it back in because it refuses to work longer than 16 hours before crapping out. I have tried updating firmware, all network resets I can. I've even tried using the old modem (we replaced both router + modem) to see if that was the root of our problems - nope, it's the router.

It has slowly been getting worse and worse, and when I am gone from this apartment my roommate will be forced to reset his router every day, sometimes twice a day, just to get internet - or purchase a new one.

I am extremely dissatisfied with this product, although not quite surprised or disappointed given its price. It just seems odd that a 3 year old Netgear N300 router performs much better than an AC1750 Dual Band router.
text_fidelity_b: TRENDnet Wireless AC1750 Dual Band Gigabit Router with USB 3.0 Share Port, Pre-Encrypted, TEW-812DRU
